tasks.spec:
You are working in freytag-forge (Python 3.12). Working directory: /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge. export PYTHONPATH=/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge TMPDIR=/tmp; run `.venv/bin/python` (never uv). Run tests with `env -u CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_URL -u CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_TOKEN .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --no-cov <files>`. No network, no live model call. Do not git commit. NEVER print or write any credential. NO regular expressions in new code. No story vocabulary (no Kristin, truck, laptop, drawer, Michelle) in non-test code. Tests may use the shipped continuity-initiative package through the helpers in tests/test_observation_mode.py (`_state_at`) and tests/test_observation_shadow.py, plus a synthetic second story. Write the tests FIRST, run them and confirm they fail for the right reason, then implement until they pass. Do not edit any file outside YOU MAY EDIT ONLY. Run ruff check and ruff format on your files at the end. BACKGROUND. RuntimeEngine._turn_active (storygame/runtime/engine.py) loops up to TURN_NARRATION_ATTEMPTS=2 times: provider call, reveal resolve, validate_effects, a deepcopy `candidate_state` with `apply_proposal(proposal, apply_world=False)`, then narration_validator.validate; a ProposalValidationError on the first attempt triggers one retry with provider.note_rejection(code). Only AFTER the loop does it call state.apply_proposal(proposal) and then WorldCapture.after_commit(command, narration, entered_scene=...), which calls ItemFactsProvider.apply_item_facts(raw, ...) and that MUTATES state.facts (World over state.facts), provider fields and makes billed model calls: one item-facts match call via CloudflareTurnProvider._request_item_facts and Jev mapping checks through the `confirm` lambda. Observation context: ItemFactsProvider._observation_context() and storygame/runtime/observation_verifier.py (ObservationVerifier, relations_from_context, fail-closed verdicts; `report.accepted` is True only when outcome is 'ok' and every verdict is 'accept'). The verifier is already built and must not change. YOU MAY EDIT ONLY: storygame/runtime/observation_preview.py (NEW), storygame/runtime/capture.py, storygame/runtime/item_facts.py (ONLY the single place described below), tests/test_observation_preview.py (NEW). 

GOAL (T8a): a side-effect-free PREVIEW of the item-fact effects on a candidate state, with the observation verifier run against the candidate, and a replay memo so the later real commit makes no second billed call. Nothing in the engine calls it yet; the product default is unchanged. 

BUILD 1. New module storygame/runtime/observation_preview.py with: (a) `class CallMemo`: records and replays answers of billed calls. `remember(kind: str, key: object, call: Callable[[], object]) -> object` returns a deepcopy of the stored answer when the same (kind, canonical JSON of key with sort_keys=True and default=str) was seen, otherwise runs `call()`, stores a deepcopy of a successful answer and returns it; an exception propagates and stores nothing (None answers are stored too). `to_json() -> dict` and `@classmethod from_json(data) -> CallMemo` (answers must be JSON-compatible; keys are strings). `hits` and `misses` integer counters. (b) `@dataclass(frozen=True) class CandidatePreview`: fields `required: bool` (an observation was required), `accepted: bool`, `outcome: str` ('not_required', 'ok', or the verifier report outcome such as 'unavailable', 'partial', 'malformed', 'budget_exhausted', or 'unrelated_move'), `failure: str | None` (generic code only: a verifier failure code or 'unrelated_move'; never narration or model text), `verdicts: tuple[dict, ...]` (thing, verdict, score), `moved_unrelated: tuple[str, ...]`, `changed: tuple[str, ...]` (sorted item names changed by the candidate), `facts_after: object` (JSON value as in the after_commit record), `command: str`, `narration: str`, `memo: CallMemo`. 

BUILD 2. In ItemFactsProvider add a public attribute `item_facts_call_memo: CallMemo | None = None` (set in __init__). In apply_item_facts, the ONE place that calls `CloudflareTurnProvider._request_item_facts(self, self._match_payload(...))` must go through the memo when set: `self.item_facts_call_memo.remember('match', payload, lambda: CloudflareTurnProvider._request_item_facts(self, payload))`; with no memo the behavior is byte-identical to today. Keep the existing except/budget-error handling around it. Build the payload once into a local variable. 

BUILD 3. In WorldCapture add `enforcing_verifier: ObservationVerifier | None = None` (separate from shadow_verifier; default None so the product is unchanged), `self._pending_preview: CandidatePreview | None = None`, and `preview_commit(self, command: str, narration: str, candidate_state, *, entered_scene: bool) -> CandidatePreview`. Behavior: if `self.enforcing_verifier is None` or `self.provider.observation_request is None`, return CandidatePreview(required=False, accepted=True, outcome='not_required', ...) without touching anything. Otherwise: take `raw = self.provider.pending_item_facts()`; remember the provider's original `state`; build a fresh CallMemo; SAVE (deepcopy) every provider turn-output field that apply_item_facts or the scene seeding touches, namely the names in WorldCapture.context() (_pending_item_facts, _pending_item_facts_present, _held_item_facts, _item_facts_issues, _changed_last_turn, _selected_names, _referred_names, _referred_lines, _last_scene_seeded, _match_offered_names, _fact_effect_snapshot, _last_item_facts_unplaced, _last_item_facts_refused, _last_item_facts_match) plus prior_steps, prior_notice_steps, command_consumed, observation_request, item_facts_seed_issues, item_facts_match_calls, item_facts_axis_fixes, item_facts_lifted, item_facts_reply_keys and _schema_cache. DO NOT save or restore the real billing counters `_turn_request_count`, `_turn_item_facts_request_count` and `request_count` (they must keep counting preview calls, because the preview really spends them). Then inside try/finally: set `provider.state = candidate_state` (a deepcopy the engine made; it is discarded afterward), set provider._schema_cache = {} (the cached schema is built from the old facts), set provider.item_facts_call_memo = memo, run the same item-fact application that after_commit performs (apply_item_facts with the same `confirm` lambda but wrapped in memo.remember('confirm', [c, s, q, st, p, k], ...), then apply_scene_placements when entered_scene, exactly as after_commit does), then build the observation context ON THE CANDIDATE with `self.provider._observation_context()`, call `self.enforcing_verifier.verify(narration, relations_from_context(context))` (do NOT call begin_turn here; before_turn does that), and compute `moved_unrelated`: names of items that existed in the real world before the preview and whose parent differs in the candidate, excluding the protagonist, the observation request's focus entity, and every thing named in the context's visible_things (and anything those contain); creations and unplaced things are not 'moved'. The finally block ALWAYS restores provider.state, all saved fields, and sets provider.item_facts_call_memo = None, even when apply_item_facts raises (a NarrationProviderError must propagate after restoration). accepted = report.accepted AND not moved_unrelated; outcome is 'unrelated_move' (failure 'unrelated_move') when the report accepted but something unrelated moved, else the report outcome. If `_observation_context()` returns None or there are no relations, accepted=True, outcome 'not_required'... but still check moved_unrelated. Store the result in `self._pending_preview` and return it. Add `take_preview(self, command: str, narration: str) -> CandidatePreview | None`: returns and clears `_pending_preview` only when its command and narration equal the arguments, else clears it and returns None. Change `after_commit` minimally: at its start call `preview = self.take_preview(command, narration)`; when preview is not None and preview.required, set `self.provider.item_facts_call_memo = preview.memo` for the duration of the existing apply (replay, so no second billed match call) and wrap `confirm` in the same memo (kind 'confirm', same key list), restoring the memo to None in a finally. Add `record['observation_preview'] = {'outcome','failure','accepted','changed','verdicts'}` only when a preview was taken and required, and `record['observation_diverged'] = True/False` comparing sorted(provider._changed_last_turn) with preview.changed and the record's facts_after with preview.facts_after (only when a preview was taken and required). With no preview the record is byte-identical to today. Also `before_turn` must call `self.enforcing_verifier.begin_turn()` when set (resets the per-turn verifier budget) and clear `_pending_preview`; `discard()` clears `_pending_preview`; keep shadow behavior unchanged and independent. 

TESTS (tests/test_observation_preview.py, hermetic, fake `ask` returning noul scores like tests/test_observation_shadow.py, real ObservationVerifier, real providers via build_capture_provider; monkeypatch CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_URL in an autouse fixture as that file does). Required cases: 1 off by default: no enforcing_verifier -> preview not required, accepted, provider untouched, ask never called. 2 EXACT RESTORATION: after preview_commit (accepted and rejected alike, and when apply_item_facts raises) `state.facts` equals a clone taken before, `provider.state is state`, and a snapshot of vars(provider) (deepcopy of every plain data attribute, excluding the three billing counters and callables) is equal before and after. This test is the guard against unknown mutated fields: make it generic over vars(provider), not over a hand list. 3 candidate really previewed: with item_facts raw that move an item, the CANDIDATE state's facts show the move (use a spy/instrumented candidate_state or the returned `changed`/`facts_after`) while the real state does not. 4 verdicts: score 1.0 -> accepted; 0.0 -> rejected with a generic failure; ask returns None -> accepted False outcome 'unavailable' (fail closed); uncertain score -> rejected; the narration text never appears in the failure or outcome. 5 unrelated move: raw item_facts that move an item nobody asked about on an observation turn -> accepted False, outcome 'unrelated_move', the unrelated name listed; a move of the protagonist or focus is allowed. 6 replay: with a fake provider network that counts match calls and a counting `ask` for Jev confirm, preview then after_commit(command, same narration) performs the billed match call and the confirm calls exactly ONCE in total (counts from the preview), the committed world equals what an unpreviewed after_commit produces on the same input, and record['observation_diverged'] is False. A different narration or command passed to after_commit drops the preview (take_preview returns None) and calls live. 7 divergence: tamper with the real state between preview and commit so the replayed application differs -> record['observation_diverged'] is True. 8 verifier turn budget: two previews in one turn after one before_turn spend two verifier requests; a third report is 'budget_exhausted' (not accepted). before_turn resets it. 9 synthetic second story: the same accept/restore/unrelated-move behavior on a tiny synthetic observatory package built like tests/test_observation_context.py does (no Kristin vocabulary). 10 shadow unchanged: with only shadow_verifier set, records are identical to before. 

FINISH: report test counts and the exact diff stat; quote preview_commit's finally block.
